title: This Swimmer Just Keeps Getting Faster — and He’s Only a College Freshman!
summary: Have you ever tried to beat your own record in something — like a video game high score or a race in the pool? Imagine doing it three times in one weekend! That’s what Koby Bujak-Upton, a super-fast swimmer from the University of Tennessee, just did at the MAC Charlotte Open. Koby, who is only a college freshman, swam in three sprint freestyle events — the 50, 100, and 200 meter races — and set new personal bests in all of them. In the 50 free, he touched the wall in 22.90 seconds, shaving off three-tenths of a second from his old record. That might not sound like much, but in swimming, it’s a huge leap! He also crushed his 100 free time (48.96 seconds) and his 200 free time (1:48.44). What makes this even cooler? Last season, Koby became the first freshman ever to swim the 200-yard freestyle in under 1 minute and 30 seconds — a barrier only nine college swimmers in history have broken. He finished second at the NCAA Championships in that event. Now, he’s heading to the Australian Trials in Sydney, where he’ll race against his country’s best for a spot on the national team. But Koby wasn’t the only star in Charlotte. A 16-year-old named David Sammons also had an amazing meet, setting personal bests in the 200 IM, 400 IM, and butterfly events. His 200 fly time even ranks him as the 9th fastest 15-16 year old in U.S. history! It just goes to show: with hard work and a love for the water, you can keep getting faster — one splash at a time.
why_it_matters: Koby's story shows that with practice and determination, you can beat your own records and move closer to big dreams, no matter how young you are.

background_read: The NCAA (National Collegiate Athletic Association) runs college sports in the U.S., and its swimming championships are where the best young swimmers compete.
Koby Bujak-Upton is originally from Australia, so he must go through the Australian Trials in Sydney to earn a spot on the national team for events like the World Championships or Olympics.
David Sammons, still a high school student, is already breaking records that place him among the fastest swimmers in U.S. history for his age group.
Article_Structure: WHO: Koby Bujak-Upton, a freshman swimmer at the University of Tennessee, and David Sammons, a 16-year-old swimmer.
WHAT: Koby set personal bests in the 50, 100, and 200 meter freestyle at the MAC Charlotte Open, and David also broke his personal records.
WHERE: At the MAC Charlotte Open in Charlotte, North Carolina.
WHY: Koby is preparing for the Australian Trials to try out for his country's national team, hoping to compete internationally.

perspectives.description: Koby's fast times prove that young athletes can compete at a high level, and he inspires other swimmers to work hard and aim for their goals.
There can be a lot of pressure on a teenager to keep breaking records, and some worry that he might burn out before reaching his full potential.
While his personal bests are impressive, he will face even faster swimmers at the Australian Trials, so his biggest tests are still ahead.
